newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea crudes mixed, quiet ahead of Aug programmes.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea crudes mixed, quiet ahead of Aug programmes.

text.p: North Sea crudes were mixed and thinly-discussed on Friday as traders opted for prudent inactivity ahead of a weekend likely to affect the future of Iraqi exports.
A cargo of Brent loading July 23-25 changed hands 13 cents weaker at a three cent discount to August Brent, reflecting a dearth of buying interest.
Talk of another Brent done at even weaker value could not be confirmed, but traders said a Forties moved at the steady value of Dated Brent +40 cents.

"The market is looking bearish for Brent. I don't see any more shorts. The market earlier this week was definitely overcooked," a trader said, referring to a premium of 10 cents over August achieved twice for Brent cargoes.
Solid North Sea prices seen this week have shaved refinery profit margins and reflect the tightness of a market still suffering the absence of Iraqi sour barrels.
But most July requirements are now covered and the focus of physical trade has shifted to August programmes, the first of which are due out on Monday.
Sunday is expected to provide strong direction to the market when the U.N. coordinator meets Iraqi officials for more talks on Baghdad's aid distribution plan.
Approval of the plan is required before Iraq can resume exports under the second phase of its oil-for-food plan.
Iraq has said it expects to resume production at a rate of between 730,000 and 750,000 bpd.

Paper markets were slow and Brent Contracts for Difference were inactive. Next week (July 14-18) was quoted at 18 cents bid with no offer, some six cents down, while July 28-01 was bid at -25 cents, again with no offer, around unchanged.
Brokers made little of the market, saying very few players were participating.
August/September Brent traded at -10 cents and -9 cents, while September/October was done at -12 cents.

Outright values firmed slightly. Front month IPE August Brent crude futures were nine cents higher at $18.01 at 1740 GMT, helped by a sharp rally in NYMEX gasoline that gave sluggish support to NYMEX crude.
Of the cargoes due to turn wet on Friday, one of two July 27-29 loaders was kept by Arcadia and the other was kept by J Aron. A July 28-30 loader was kept by Arcadia.
In the Med, the delay in resuming exports of Iraqi Kirkuk has raised the price of sour crudes and left some refiners, Turkey's Tupras included, searching for alternatives.
Sour crudes in the Med are also drawing strength from a Turkish tender.

Other grades offered into the tender are thought to include Syrian Light at around Dated Brent -35 cents a barrel, some 20 cents firmer than the July Official Selling Price (OSP), and Iranian Heavy at higher than Dated Brent -$1.80 a barrel.
-- W Maclean, M Thompson London newsroom +44 171 542 7646
